name: SonarQube
description: Self-hosted SonarQube Server reads: instance status and health, the projects the token can administrate, one project's quality measures, its open issues, the instance's quality gates and its metric dictionary. Read-only; issue transitions, quality-gate editing, project provisioning and the whole /api/system restart and migration surface are deliberately absent.

tools.name: system_status
tools.description: Get the running status of the SonarQube instance this credential points at: id, version and status (STARTING, UP, DOWN, RESTARTING, DB_MIGRATION_NEEDED, DB_MIGRATION_RUNNING)

tools.name: system_health
tools.description: Get the health status of the SonarQube instance: GREEN (fully operational), YELLOW (usable but needs attention) or RED (not operational), with the causes and per-application-node detail. Requires the token's user to hold 'Administer System'

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the projects on this SonarQube instance (key, name, visibility, last analysis date, analysed revision). Requires the token's user to hold 'Administer System'

q.description: Optional search string; matches project names and project keys that contain it

tools.name: project_measures
tools.description: Get the current quality measures for one SonarQube component: bugs, vulnerabilities, code smells and coverage. A metric with no analysis is absent from the list rather than zero

component.description: Component key: a project key from list_projects, or a file key within it (e.g. quoxproof-live)

branch.description: Optional branch name; the main branch is used when omitted

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: Search issues on this SonarQube instance, optionally narrowed to given components, impact severities or issue statuses (rule, severity, status, file, line, message, effort)

components.description: Optional comma-separated component keys to scope the search to (a project key, or a file key within it)

impact_severities.description: Optional comma-separated impact severities: INFO, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, BLOCKER

issue_statuses.description: Optional comma-separated issue statuses: OPEN, CONFIRMED, FALSE_POSITIVE, ACCEPTED, FIXED

resolved.description: Optional: true returns only resolved issues, false only unresolved

tools.name: list_quality_gates
tools.description: List the quality gates configured on this SonarQube instance, with which one is the default, which are built in, and each gate's clean-as-you-code compliance status

tools.name: list_metrics
tools.description: List the metric keys this SonarQube instance knows about (key, name, type, domain, direction), which is what project_measures accepts as metric keys

needs_review: AUTH KEPT AS SCAFFOLDED, AND THE VENDOR DOCS STILL DOCUMENT IT: basic with userField token and passField "" sends base64(token + ':'), which is byte-identical to the vault entry integrationTypeRegistry.js key sonarqube, whose testHeaders is ``'Authorization': `Basic ${Buffer.from(`${creds.token}:`).toString('base64')}```, and whose testEndpoint is base_url + /api/authentication/validate, this spec's test block verbatim. Managing your tokens (https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/latest/user-guide/managing-tokens/, fetched 2026-09-12) says verbatim: 'when invoking web services, pass the token using the bearer or basic HTTP authentication scheme, see Web API.' followed by 'In both cases, you don't need to provide a password.' The token is therefore the basic-auth USERNAME with an empty password, which is exactly what passField "" expresses (the same form tailscale uses). Note for later: the Web API page (https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/latest/extension-guide/web-api/) says 'To authenticate to the Web API, we recommend that you use the bearer authentication scheme', so bearer with the same token is the vendor-preferred alternative. Basic is kept because it is still documented as supported AND it is the form the vault already proves against; switching to bearer would silently diverge the connector from the credential test.

CATEGORY CHANGED FROM 'security' TO 'developer': the scaffold wrote 'security', which is NOT one of the twelve values in use across this spec directory (cloud_hosting, commerce_finance, communication, crm_sales, data_ai, developer, files_knowledge, hr_hiring, marketing_email, media, monitoring, project_management). The vault entry also says 'developer', and the sibling connector sonarcloud.connector.json is 'developer', so SonarQube sits with the other code-quality and source control planes rather than inventing a thirteenth value.

PATHS, PARAMS AND CLAMPS COME FROM THE LIVE SELF-DESCRIBING REGISTRY, NOT FROM MEMORY: https://next.sonarqube.com/sonarqube/api/webservices/list (SonarSource's public SonarQube Server, version 2026.5.0.130905, fetched anonymously 2026-09-12, 200). Verbatim from it: api/projects/search is 'Search for projects or views to administrate them. ... Requires 'Administer System' permission' with ps defaultValue 100 maximumValue 500; api/system/health is 'Provide health status of SonarQube. ... Requires the 'Administer System' permission or system passcode (see sonar.web.systemPasscode in sonar.properties).'; api/measures/component is 'Return component with specified measures.' with component and metricKeys both required=true; api/issues/search is 'Search for issues. Requires the 'Browse' permission on the specified project(s).' with ps defaultValue 100 maximumValue 500; api/metrics/search ps defaultValue 100 maximumValue 500. Hence clamp 100 500 on all three paged tools, and the input descriptions state the vendor default and cap.

TWO TOOLS NEED AN ADMIN TOKEN, SO THE LIVE HARNESS MUST MINT ONE FOR AN ADMINISTRATOR: list_projects and system_health both require 'Administer System' per the registry lines quoted above, proven live 2026-09-12 by calling them anonymously on next.sonarqube.com and getting 403 {"errors":[{"msg":"Insufficient privileges"}]} from both. system_status is public (200 {"id":...,"version":"2026.5.0.130905","status":"UP"} with no credential at all), which makes it the one tool that proves reachability independently of permissions.

RESPONSE SHAPES ARE EVIDENCED, NOT GUESSED. Proven live against next.sonarqube.com on 2026-09-12: /api/system/status returned {"id","version","status"}; /api/metrics/search?ps=2 returned {"metrics":[{"id","key","type","name","description","domain","direction","qualitative","hidden"}],"total","p","ps"}; /api/qualitygates/list returned {"qualitygates":[{"name","isDefault","isBuiltIn","actions","caycStatus","hasStandardConditions","hasMQRConditions","isAiCodeSupported"}]}; /api/measures/component?component=<public project>&metricKeys=ncloc,bugs,code_smells returned {"component":{"key","name","qualifier","measures":[{"metric","value","bestValue"}]}}; /api/issues/search?components=<public project>&ps=1 returned {"total","p","ps","paging","effortTotal","issues":[{"key","rule","severity","component","project","line","status","message","effort","type","issueStatus","creationDate","updateDate",...}],"components":[...]}. The two admin-only shapes come from the instance's own published response examples (/api/webservices/response_example): projects/search gives {"paging":{"pageIndex","pageSize","total"},"components":[{"key","name","qualifier","visibility","lastAnalysisDate","revision","managed","projectUuid"}]} and system/health gives {"health","causes":[{"message"}],"nodes":[{"name","type","host","port","startedAt","health","causes"}]}.

QUALITY GATES NO LONGER CARRY AN id, SO NONE IS PICKED: on 2026.5 the qualitygates/list items are keyed by name only (the live body above has no id field at all), where SonarQube 9.x and 10.x returned one. Picking a dropped field would have produced a permanently absent key, so the pick is name, isDefault, isBuiltIn, caycStatus and isAiCodeSupported. The per-gate 'actions' object is deliberately skipped: it describes what the CALLER could mutate, which is meaningless in a read-only connector and pure token cost.

METRIC SET IS A FIXED LITERAL, MATCHING THE sonarcloud SIBLING: metricKeys is required=true and spec v1.1 has no default-value helper (clamp is the only helper and it is numeric), so an optional metric_keys input would render empty, be dropped from the query, and 400 the call. project_measures therefore hard-codes bugs,vulnerabilities,code_smells,coverage, exactly as sonarcloud.connector.json does, and list_metrics exists so a caller can discover what else the instance knows.

BASE URL IS CUSTOMER-SUPPLIED, SO NOTHING HERE IS PROVABLE BLIND: SonarQube Server is self-hosted, base_url comes from the credential ({fromCredential: 'base_url'}), and the paths above were exercised against SonarSource's own public instance rather than the customer's. This spec is NOT SHAPE_PROVEN by a blind 401 sweep; it is marked for the live harness, which stands up an ephemeral SonarQube container, mints an administrator user token, and provisions a project keyed quoxproof-live.

PROBES RESOLVE ON A FRESH INSTANCE, BY CONSTRUCTION: system_status, system_health, list_projects, list_quality_gates carry an empty or numeric-only _probe because they need no resource (a fresh instance already has its built-in quality gates and its full metric dictionary). project_measures and list_issues are the only tools that name a resource, and both probe the provisioner's project key quoxproof-live. RISK TO WATCH IN THE LIVE RUN: a project that has been provisioned but never analysed has no measures, so /api/measures/component may answer 404 'Component key not found' rather than 200 with an empty measures array, and /api/issues/search answers 200 with issues: [] but returns 503 while issue indexing is still in progress (the registry text says so verbatim). Neither is a spec defect; both are timing facts the harness must handle, by analysing once or by retrying.

READ-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THE OMISSIONS ARE THE POINT: all seven tools are GETs. The same Web API exposes POST on issues (do_transition, assign, add_comment, set_severity), quality gate create/copy/destroy and condition editing, projects create/delete/bulk_delete, permission grants, user and token management, and the /api/system restart, migrate_db and logs surface. None is wired here. Nothing in this connector may be described as managing or remediating a SonarQube instance.
